title: A closed immersion into projective space supplies an ample invertible sheaf
statement: Let $A$ be a ring, let $n\ge0$, let $\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}=\operatorname{Proj}(\mathbf Z[T_0,\dots,T_n])$ ($\deg T_k=1$) and $\mathbf P^n_A=\mathbf P(\{0,\dots,n\};\operatorname{Spec}A)=\operatorname{Spec}A\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], with projections $q:\mathbf P^n_A\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $\rho:\mathbf P^n_A\to\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$. Let $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}}(1)=\widetilde{S(1)}$ be the twisting sheaf of $\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] with its global sections $T_0,\dots,T_n$, and put $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^n_A}(1)=\rho^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}}(1)$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. Let $X$ be a scheme with a morphism $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ and a closed immersion $i:X\to\mathbf P^n_A$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] with $q\circ i=f$. Then $\mathcal L=i^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^n_A}(1)$ is an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] which is ample on $X$ in the absolute sense of Stacks Definition 01PS [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]; more precisely $X$ is quasi-compact, and for the sections $s_k=i^*\rho^*T_k\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L)$ ($k=0,\dots,n$) the non-vanishing loci $X_{s_k}$ are affine open subschemes covering $X$. (Since $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is affine, 'ample on $X$' is the same as '$f$-ample' in the sense of Stacks Morphisms Definition 01VH, by Morphisms Lemma 01VK; only the absolute notion is asserted and used here.)

source.place: Properties, Definition 01PS (definition-ample) and Lemma 01PU (lemma-ample-on-closed) with its proof; Constructions, Definition 01NF (definition-projective-space), Lemma 01NG (lemma-standard-covering-projective-space), Definition 01MN (definition-twist), Lemma 01MW (lemma-ample-on-proj); Morphisms, Definition 01VH and Lemma 01VK (lemma-ample-over-affine) for the remark on f-ampleness; Morphisms Lemma 01W9 (lemma-H-projective) for the setting

proof.text: *Comparison of the two twisting sheaves.* Let $\mathcal O^{\mathrm{gl}}(1)$ be the module of [def-pc-projective-space-twist] on $\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ ($A=\mathbf Z$, $d=1$, index set $\{0,\dots,n\}$) with its global sections $T^{\mathrm{gl}}_k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-twist-glued-identification] there is an isomorphism $\theta:\mathcal O^{\mathrm{gl}}(1)\to\widetilde{S(1)}=\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}}(1)$ with $\theta(T^{\mathrm{gl}}_k)=T_k$. Applying the functor $\rho^*$ [def-pc-module-pullback] gives an isomorphism $\rho^*\theta:\rho^*\mathcal O^{\mathrm{gl}}(1)\to\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^n_A}(1)$ carrying $\rho^*T^{\mathrm{gl}}_k$ to $\rho^*T_k$ (a functor carries isomorphisms to isomorphisms, and pullback of sections is natural), and then $i^*\rho^*\theta$ identifies $i^*\rho^*\mathcal O^{\mathrm{gl}}(1)$ with $\mathcal L$, carrying $i^*\rho^*T^{\mathrm{gl}}_k$ to $s_k$. So it suffices to prove every assertion for $\mathcal O_P(1)=\rho^*\mathcal O^{\mathrm{gl}}(1)$ and its sections $T_k$, which is the module of [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts] for $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$; write $P=\mathbf P^n_A$, $D_+(T_k)_S=\rho^{-1}(D_+(T_k))$ and $u_{l/k}$ as there.

source.place: Constructions, Definition 01MN (definition-twist) and Lemma 01NG; the identification of the glued and the $\widetilde{S(1)}$ twisting sheaf

proof.text: *$\mathcal L$ is invertible.* Put $X_k=i^{-1}(D_+(T_k)_S)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts] (a) the $D_+(T_k)_S$ cover $P$, so the $X_k$ cover $X$. By (b) of that lemma applied to $g=i:X\to P$, the section $s_k=i^*T_k$ is a free generator of $\mathcal L=i^*\mathcal O_P(1)$ over $X_k$: for every open $V\subseteq X_k$ the map $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_X)\to\Gamma(V,\mathcal L)$, $a\mapsto a\,s_k|_V$, is bijective, i.e. $\mathcal O_{X_k}\to\mathcal L|_{X_k}$, $a\mapsto as_k$, is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{X_k}$-modules. Hence $\mathcal L$ is locally free of rank one, and quasi-coherent (being locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_X$), i.e. invertible [def-sc-invertible-module].

source.place: Constructions, Lemma 01NG (lemma-standard-covering-projective-space), Definition 01NF and the discussion after it ($\mathcal L=\varphi^*\mathcal O(1)$, $s_i=\varphi^*T_i$)

proof.text:
*The non-vanishing loci: $X_{s_k}=X_k$.* For $x\in X$ the value of $s_k$ at $x$ is its image in $\mathcal L_x\otimes\kappa(x)$, as in [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] (with $\mathcal L^{\otimes1}=\mathcal L$). If $x\in X_k$, $s_k$ generates the free rank-one module $\mathcal L_x$ (Step 2), so its value is a basis of the one-dimensional $\kappa(x)$-vector space $\mathcal L_x\otimes\kappa(x)$, hence nonzero: $X_k\subseteq X_{s_k}$. Conversely let $x
otin X_k$, $p=i(x)
otin D_+(T_k)_S$, and choose $j$ with $x\in X_j$ (Step 2). By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts] (b) for $g=\mathrm{id}_P$, $T_k=u_{k/j}T_j$ on $D_+(T_j)_S$, $T_j$ is a generator there, and $P_{T_k}=D_+(T_k)_S$; so $0=T_k(p)=u_{k/j}(p)\,T_j(p)$ with $T_j(p)
eq0$, whence $u_{k/j}(p)=0$ in $\kappa(p)$. By (b) for $g=i$, $s_k=i^*(u_{k/j})\,s_j$ on $X_j$, and the value of the function $i^*(u_{k/j})$ at $x$ is the image of $u_{k/j}(p)=0$ under $\kappa(p)	o\kappa(x)$ (the stalk map of $i$ is local), so $s_k(x)=0$. Thus $X_{s_k}=X_k$.

source.place: Constructions, Lemma 01NG (lemma-standard-covering-projective-space), Definition 01NF and the discussion after it ($\mathcal L=\varphi^*\mathcal O(1)$, $s_i=\varphi^*T_i$)

proof.text: *Each $X_{s_k}$ is affine.* By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts] (c) for the affine open $S'=S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ (so $q^{-1}(S')=P$), $D_+(T_k)_S$ is affine, $\cong\operatorname{Spec}A[U_l:l\neq k]$. Since $i$ is a closed immersion, by the affine form of [def-weil-closed-immersion] (Stacks 01QO) the preimage of the affine open $D_+(T_k)_S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$ for an ideal $I$, so $X_{s_k}=X_k=i^{-1}(D_+(T_k)_S)$ is an affine open subscheme of $X$ (Stacks Schemes 01IH, used in the proof of Properties 01PU).

*$\mathcal L$ is ample.* $X=X_{s_0}\cup\dots\cup X_{s_n}$ is a finite union of affine schemes, each quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact] (iii); a finite union of quasi-compact subspaces is quasi-compact, so $X$ is quasi-compact, condition (1) of [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. For $x\in X$ choose $k$ with $x\in X_{s_k}$; then $s_k\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L^{\otimes1})$ and $X_{s_k}$ is affine (Step 4), which is condition (2) with exponent $1$. Hence $\mathcal L$ is ample. (For the remark: $f=q\circ i$ with $\operatorname{Spec}A$ affine, so by Stacks Morphisms Lemma 01VK this is the same as $\mathcal L$ being $f$-ample in the sense of Morphisms Definition 01VH; no node asserts or needs that relative notion.)

split_report.summary: Statement repaired as the lead_note asked: the citation def-sc-ample (ampleness over a field) is replaced by def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module (absolute ampleness, Stacks 01PS), and the conclusion is now 'L is invertible and ample on X' (with the explicit affine cover X_{s_k}), which is what lem-weil-pbc-coherent-twist-global-generation needs; f-ampleness (01VH) is mentioned only as a remark (equal to ampleness over affine Spec A by 01VK, not 01VG which is a section tag). The statement now introduces O_{P^n_A}(1) explicitly as rho^* of the twisting sheaf of P^n_Z (def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf is for Proj of a graded ring, while P^n_A is the base change of def-nagata-projective-space-base-change), adding def-pc-module-pullback. The source place 01Q1 (open immersion into Proj(Gamma_*)) did not prove this and was replaced by 01PU (ample restricts to closed subschemes) with 01NG. Proof in five steps: identification of the glued and the S(1)-tilde twisting sheaf, invertibility and the non-vanishing loci via the standard-chart lemma, affineness of the charts and of their preimages under the closed immersion, then Definition 01PS with exponent 1. No new nodes.
